rationale.complete: Rounds 1 and 1b done; round 2 (2026-10-05) tested the three redirects (attachment kernel, stigmergy vs chat, herding and output) on 40 units with synthetic validation on real skeletons, pre-registration and amendments A1 (pre-data) and A2 (post hoc). The frozen holdout test and a call-clock join test are not run.
rationale.faithfulness: The Potts sign rule failed; round 2 finds a sublinear, time-symmetric join kernel that replays the work size distribution in 10/13 units but cannot be read as causal attachment (lag = lead), and refutes stigmergy. Drive and coupling are still not separated at the 30-min scale.
rationale.usefulness: Operator numbers: a shared project's commits grow as n^0.70 with the agents on it (each extra agent adds about 0.7 of a solo agent), herding does not cut a herded agent's own rate, and chat (not the artifact record) steers pile-ons.

one_line: Agents pile onto projects in same-hour bursts steered by chat, not the artifact record; a shared project's commits grow as n^0.70 with its agents.

v2.claim: Herding is not stigmergic: in 37 non-reserved units, other agents' commits to a project never predict an agent's join better than read chat mentions of it (held-out ΔLL_CM pooled −0.047 [−0.070, −0.024] in 24 attention units and −0.002 [−0.026, +0.023] in 13 work units, where synthetic artifact-driven worlds give ΔLL_CM > 0 in ≥ 88% of runs; pooled join OR for a read chat mention 3.0 vs 1.26 for commits in attention, 2.2 vs 1.8 in work). Excluded (rule 1): θ = 0.70 (attention-defined n includes watchers; the card's own round-3 redirect recomputes it); 'excluding past-driven attachment' (post hoc A2 power 0.38–1.0); the sublinear α kernel (scored separately it is ≈ 0.75 but is not this clause).
v2.decision: operator lever: a shared project's output grows as n^0.7; split work across owned artifacts; steer joins through chat, not artifacts
v2.generality: multi-agent LLM swarms with shared repos
